study.title: The altered hypothalamic network functional connectivity in chronic insomnia disorder and regulation effect of acupuncture: a randomized controlled neuroimaging study
study.study_design: Two-experiment study: a cross-sectional and a longitudinal experiment. The longitudinal experiment was a randomized controlled trial.
study.randomization: CID patients randomly assigned to one of two groups according to a table of random numbers generated using SAS 9.2 software by a researcher not involved in patient recruitment and treatment.
study.blinding: Grouping information was blind for CID patients, recruiting researchers, and statisticians. Acupuncturists were not blinded.
study.population: Patients with chronic insomnia disorder (CID) recruited from the hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (CDUTCM), Chengdu second people hospital, and via online advertisements; and matched healthy controls (HCs).
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) be of any gender, between 18 and 65 years of age, and right-handed; (2) meet the diagnostic criteria of ICSD-3 and have experienced difficulty with falling asleep, staying asleep, or early awakening for a minimum of three months; (3) meet the diagnosis of spleen and stomach disharmony in Chinese medicine; (4) have a score of 7 or above on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI); and (5) sign an informed consent form to voluntarily participate in the study. HCs: (1) reporting good sleep quality; (2) passing neuropsychological tests; and (3) passing a physical examination without any functional or organic disease or a history of head injury.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) serious primary diseases affecting the liver, kidney, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, or hematopoietic systems; (2) a history of other neuropsychiatric disorders, such as major depression or generalized anxiety; (3) systemic illnesses, such as pain, fever, cough, or surgery; (4) insomnia resulting from alcohol and/or psychotropic substance abuse and dependence, including the use of sleeping pills; (5) significant headache, migraine, or history of head trauma; (6) recent use of antibiotics, glucocorticoids, immunosuppressants, or herbal medicines within the past month; (7) pregnancy, preparation for pregnancy, or breastfeeding; (8) typical contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning, such as claustrophobia; or (9) participation in another clinical trial within the past month. HCs: same as for patients with CID.

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle inserted at non-acupoints to a depth of 2–3 mm, which falls within the superficial skin-only range (1–5 mm). At this depth, only cutaneous Aβ/Aδ fibers are engaged; muscle and fascia are not reached. No manipulation was performed, but depth alone determines the level.

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI; participants instructed to close their eyes, remain still and quiet, avoid any head movements, remain awake, and try not to think about anything
resting-state fMRI; after completion of real acupuncture treatment
resting-state fMRI; after completion of sham acupuncture treatment
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Identical sham procedure to the baseline condition: needle inserted at non-acupoints to 2–3 mm depth, engaging only superficial cutaneous tissue. This is within the 1–5 mm superficial range, classifying as Level 2 regardless of the absence of needle manipulation.

interventions.manipulation_exact: gently twisted, lifted, and pushed the needles with consistent amplitude, force, and speed to induce the Deqi sensation
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; Deqi refers to the subjective feelings of soreness, numbness, heaviness, and distension experienced by the patient, as well as the sensations of heaviness, astringency, and tightness felt by the acupuncturist
interventions.treatment_period_exact: four-week treatment duration, with five consecutive daily sessions per week followed by two days off
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to traditional acupuncture practices and several clinical studies; DU20 is a commonly used acupoint to improve sleep; RN12 and ST36 are commonly used to regulate gastrointestinal function; ST36 can regulate not only GI symptoms but also sleep; selected according to a previous similar study on disharmony of stomach theory

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: non-acupoints located near the real acupoints (2 cm lateral to DU20, RN12, and ST36), which were not part of any known meridian or traditional acupoint
interventions.manipulation_exact: After the needle was inserted into the skin, no needle manipulation was performed
interventions.treatment_period_exact: four-week treatment duration, with five consecutive daily sessions per week followed by two days off
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Referring to a previous study [33], the SA group adopted the operation method of shallow needle insertion (depth of 2–3 mm) at non-acupoints.

sham_details.sham_location_exact: non-acupoints located 2 cm lateral to DU20, RN12, and ST36, which were not part of any known meridian or traditional acupoint
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: no needle manipulation was performed after insertion

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: Deqi sensation (soreness, numbness, heaviness, distension experienced by patient; heaviness, astringency, tightness felt by acupuncturist)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was described as intended and required before needle retention; no quantitative deqi scores reported

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Structural: high-resolution T1-weighted brain volume MRI sequence; Functional: echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Functional: total volume of 255 (TR=2000 ms, 35 slices); first 10 volumes removed
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: DPARSF (http://rfmri.org) and SPM 12 (www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm) in MATLAB 2014b (MathWorks, Natick, MA)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: DPARSF, SPM 12, MATLAB 2014b; AFNI (3dFWHMx and 3dClustSim) for Monte Carlo simulations
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: isotropic Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum of 6 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: excluded if head motion >2 mm or 2°
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: bandpass filter with a range of 0.01–0.08 Hz
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: regression of nuisance signals such as global mean, white matter, cerebrospinal fluid signal, and six motion parameters
statistical_thresholds_exact: p<0.005 at the voxel level and p<0.05 at the cluster level, corrected for false discovery rate (FDR)
minimum voxel value set to 20 in FDR-corrected clusters
If results did not survive FDR correction, small volume correction applied using Monte Carlo simulations (3dFWHMx and 3dClustSim) to disease-related ROIs
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: False discovery rate (FDR) correction at cluster level (p<0.05); if not surviving FDR, Monte Carlo simulation-based small volume correction applied to ROIs defined using Anatomical Automated Labeling Atlas

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative deqi/sensory scores are reported. The paper describes deqi as intended and required for RA, but no formal measurement instrument (e.g., MASS, SASI, VAS) or numerical deqi scores are provided for either RA or SA groups.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success (participant guessing of allocation) are not reported or assessed in this paper.
Adverse events are not reported in this paper. No section on adverse events or safety outcomes is included.

The paper reports depth as '0.5 to 1.5 cun' for RA. The paper defines 1 cun = 25 mm, so the range is 12.5–37.5 mm, but specific numeric values per acupoint are not given. depth_mm_numeric was left null as a range is stated.

Table 2 reports SDS_baseline as 45.00(10.5) for RA and 28.35(8.00) for SA with p=0.32 (F/T/X2=1.01), which seems unusually different for a 'not significant' comparison. This may reflect a typographical error in the paper. Extracted as reported.

The paper references Figure S1 (hypothalamus ROI locations), Figure S2 (LH rsFC at lenient threshold), Figure S3 (uncorrected between-group ANOVA results), and Supplementary Materials (Chinese medicine diagnosis criteria). These supplement figures are not provided in the PDF and their data cannot be extracted.

The 2-way ANOVA between RA and SA groups for the between-group hypothalamus rsFC comparison: the paper states 'There was no significant effects of group and treatment on the hypothalamus rsFC network after correction for multiple comparisons. The uncorrected results are presented in Figure S3.' The Table 3 rows labeled 'Different changes between the two treatment groups' appear to be uncorrected or survived a different threshold. The correction status of these rows requires clarification.
The n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging field was set to 65 (42 CID + 23 HCs for cross-sectional), though the longitudinal neuroimaging includes 37 (18 RA + 19 SA). These represent separate analyses.

LH rsFC results in the longitudinal experiment (RA and SA post vs. pre, RA vs. SA) are not reported in Table 3 or the main text. The paper states LH showed no significant differences vs. HCs at the set threshold; longitudinal LH results are not mentioned.

The paper reports PSQI_change for RA as 4.61(2.73) and SA as 2.16(2.81), labeled 't=2.69, p=0.01' under between-group comparison (Table 2), but the statistical test column header shows F/T/X2, suggesting this could be a t-statistic. Extracted as reported.

Sample sizes for the RA and SA groups in Table 2 appear to be n=18 and n=19 respectively (final analyzed), but Table 1 uses n=42 CID patients for the cross-sectional analysis. The n_analyzed values in the neural results for within-group longitudinal analyses were set accordingly.

The conjunction analysis spatial overlap described in Figure 3 and the text is a qualitative/visual overlap, not a formal statistical conjunction (e.g., minimum t-statistic conjunction). No quantitative threshold for the overlap is reported beyond 'overlapped.'
